classification.difficultyReason: Expand two shifted functions and simplify exact surd coefficients for the final transformation.

content.prompt: Convert $\cos\left(\theta-\frac{2\pi}3\right)+\sin\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}3\right)$ to an appropriate auxiliary-angle form.

answer.short:
$\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{2}\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi4\right)$.

Expand both functions and collect equal sine and cosine coefficients.
answer.worked:
Let $g(\theta)=\cos\left(\theta-\frac{2\pi}3\right)+\sin\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}3\right)$.
$$\begin{align*}g(\theta)&=-\frac12\cos\theta+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin\theta-\frac12\sin\theta+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cos\theta\\g(\theta)&=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2}\cos\theta+\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2}\sin\theta.\end{align*}$$
For $R\cos(\theta-\alpha)$, the equal positive coefficients give $\alpha=\frac\pi4$.
$$\begin{align*}R&=\sqrt{2\left(\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2}\right)^2}\\R&=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{2}\\g(\theta)&=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{2}\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi4\right).\end{align*}$$
